text.p: ImmuDyne Inc said on Thursday that it reached an agreement in principal for the settlement of a shareholder lawsuit.
The lawsuit was brought by shareholders Mark McLaughlin and Thomas McCarvill. A counter suit was filed by the company, a major shareholder and its president James Woods, the company said.

In the settlement agreement, ImmuDyne; Carmel Research Inc, an ImmuDyne shareholder; Byron Donzis, an ImmuDyne shareholder; James Wood; Mark McLaughlin and Thomas McCarvill, agree that they will use their best efforts to make ImmuDyne a profitable venture and maximize sales, ImmuDyne said.
Under the terms of the settlement, royalty payments paid by ImmuDyne to its shareholder, Carmel Research, for licensing of patents and related technology will decrease from 12 percent to 10 percent.
As part of the deal, ImmuDyne's shares outstanding will decrease, on a net basis, by 1.7 million.
Carmel research also agreed to transfer 3.25 million shares of ImmuDyne stock to ImmuDyne. ImmuDyne also agreed to transfer to McLaughlin and his attorneys 1.55 million shares of ImmuDyne stock.

In addition, under the terms of the settlement, $500,000 will be paid to McLaughlin and his attorneys from royalties otherwise due to Carmel and a representative of McLaughlin will be appointed to ImmuDyne's Board of Directors.
Donzis, who remains a significant shareholder, has resigned as consultant to ImmuDyne.
The agreement is subject to confirmation by the court following a hearing.

The settlement also is subject to ImmuDyne entering into an arms length distribution agreement with Nutrition Supply Corp, the company said. While the parties have engaged in discussions, to date they have been unable to reach an agreement.
